How do I specify termination for mutually recursive function that are defined via a type alias that hides the decreasing argument?

E.g. I have

def Parser (α : Type) := (toks:List Token)
  → Except String (α × List Token)

and

mutual
  inductive Field where
    | Field : String → Expression → Field

  inductive Expression where
    | List : List Expression -> Expression
    | StrLit : String -> Expression
    | NatLit : Nat -> Expression
    | Id : String -> Expression
    | Constructor : String -> List Field → Expression
end

Then I need

mutual
  def parseField : Parser Field

  def parseFields : Parser (List Field)

  def parseExpressions : Parser (List Expression)

  def parseExpression : Parser Expression

end

and I don't know how to proceed to give good hints for termination condition.

(I can give the detailed functions, but I suspect there is just a pattern that I need to follow so I'll ask it like this...)

Thanks!

Could you provide a #mwe of your issue? Perhaps not all constructors and functions are needed to surface your problem?

In general Lean can provide termination of recursive definitions, e.g.,

mutual

inductive A where
  | bot : A
  | fromB : B → A
deriving Repr

inductive B where
  | bot : B
  | fromA : A → B
deriving Repr

end

inductive Token where
  | botA
  | botB
  | fromA
  | fromB
deriving Repr

abbrev Parser (α : Type) :=
  List Token → Except String (α × List Token)

mutual

def parseA : Parser A := fun xs =>
  match xs with
  | .botA :: xs => .ok (A.bot, xs)
  | .fromB :: xs => do
    let (b, xs) ← parseB xs
    .ok (.fromB b, xs)
  | _ => .error "failed to parse A"

def parseB : Parser B := fun xs =>
  match xs with
  | .botB :: xs => .ok (B.bot, xs)
  | .fromA :: xs => do
    let (a, xs) ← parseA xs
    .ok (.fromA a, xs)
  | _ => .error "failed to parse B"

end

def ok : List Token := [.fromA, .botA]

#eval parseB ok

def notOk : List Token := [.fromA, .botB]

#eval parseB notOk

Hi -- thanks! ...trying to work out exactly what is different about your code.

Well, one thing that I forgot to mention is that I defined a Monad instance for Parser and am using that.

I've whittled the code down a bit so here is a closer-to-minimal working example:

inductive Token
  | strLit (s : String)
  | lbracket
  | rbracket
deriving Repr, BEq

inductive Expression where
    | List : List Expression -> Expression
    | StrLit : String -> Expression

def Parser (α : Type) := (toks:List Token)
  → Except String (α × List Token)

instance : Monad Parser where
  pure a := fun toks => Except.ok (a, toks)
  bind p f := fun toks => do
    let (a, toks') ← p toks
    f a toks'

mutual
  def parseExpression : Parser Expression
  | [] => Except.error "nothing to parse"
  | tok :: rest  => match tok with
    | Token.strLit s => Except.ok (Expression.StrLit s, rest)
    | Token.lbracket => do
      let (exprs,toks') ← parseExpressions rest
      pure (Expression.List exprs,toks')
    | _ =>
      Except.error "mal-formed"


  def parseExpressions : Parser (List Expression) :=
      fun toks => pexprs toks []
    where
      pexprs (toks : List Token) (acc : List Expression)
          : Except String (List Expression × List Token) :=
        match toks with
        | [] => Except.ok (acc.reverse,[])
        | tok::rest =>
        match tok with
        | Token.rbracket =>
          Except.ok (acc.reverse,rest)
        | _ => do
          let (expr, toks') ← parseExpression toks
          pexprs toks' (expr :: acc)
end

And: it works with a fuel argument.

inductive Token where
  | strLit (s : String)
  | lbracket
  | rbracket
deriving Repr, BEq

inductive Expression where
    | List : List Expression -> Expression
    | StrLit : String -> Expression
deriving Repr

abbrev Parser (α : Type) :=
  (toks : List Token) → Except String (α × List Token)

mutual
  def parseExpression (fuel : Nat) : Parser Expression := fun toks =>
    match fuel with
    | 0 => .error "out of fuel"
    | n+1 =>
      match toks with
      | .strLit s :: rest => .ok (.StrLit s, rest)
      | .lbracket :: rest  => do
          let (exprs,toks') ← parseExpressions n [] rest
          pure (.List exprs,toks')
      | _ => .error "failed to parse expr"

  def parseExpressions (fuel : Nat) (accum : List Expression)
      : Parser (List Expression) := fun toks =>
    match fuel with
    | 0 => .error "out of fuel"
    | n+1 => match toks with
      | [] => .error "failed to parse expression list"
      | .rbracket :: rest => .ok (accum.reverse,rest)
      | _  => do
          let (expr, rest') ← parseExpression n toks
          parseExpressions n (expr::accum) rest'

end

def test : List Token := [ .lbracket
  , .strLit "foo"
  , .strLit "a"
  , .lbracket
  , .strLit "in the inner list"
  , .rbracket
  , .rbracket ]

#eval parseExpression test.length test

George McNinch said:

Anyhow, here is a shorter mwe of my troubles:

It is quite interesting.

If you use termination_by toks => toks.length you can see that the goal failed to be proved is

head✝ : Token
rest : List Token
rest' : List Token
⊢ rest'.length < (head✝ :: rest).length

so the problem is that Lean at that point knows no relation between rest and rest'.

One solution, which is probably quite cumbersome for your use case, is to make the parser produce a proof that the length of the rest is strictly decreasing.

inductive Token where
  | strLit (s : String)
  | lbracket
  | rbracket
deriving Repr, BEq

inductive Expression where
    | List : List Expression -> Expression
    | StrLit : String -> Expression

abbrev Parser (α : Type) :=
    (toks : List Token)
    →
    Except String
    { -- Subtype
       result : (α × List Token)
      // result.snd.length < toks.length
    }

mutual
  def parseExpression : Parser Expression := fun toks =>
    match h : toks with
    | .strLit s :: rest => .ok ⟨(.StrLit s, rest), by grind⟩
    | .lbracket :: rest  => do
      let ⟨(exprs, toks'), _⟩ ← parseExpressions [] rest
      pure ⟨(.List exprs, toks'), by grind⟩
    | _ => .error "failed to parse expr"
  termination_by toks => toks.length

  def parseExpressions (accum : List Expression)
      : Parser (List Expression) := fun toks =>
    match toks with
    | .rbracket :: rest => .ok ⟨(accum.reverse, rest), by grind⟩
    | _ :: rest => do
      let ⟨(expr, rest'), h⟩ ← parseExpression rest
      let ⟨(exprs, rest''), h'⟩ ← parseExpressions (expr :: accum) rest'
      -- Are there performance implications here?
      .ok ⟨(exprs, rest''), by grind⟩
    | [] => .error "failed to parse expression list"
  termination_by toks => toks.length
  decreasing_by
    · grind
    · grind
end

Maybe somebody else knows of an easier way to inject this information such that the proof of decreasing measure goes through. (As far as I know it is not possible to write "theorems" about mutual definitions in their defining block.)
